findings.reason: The protected source is an expert-quality linear trie solution: a precise collision signature partitions independent words, per-prefix counts locate the first distinguishing character, and one final omitted-length check implements the no-longer abbreviation rule. Its two-pass structure and algorithmic names are direct, so no inert candidate is materially justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 527 and its Python list-of-words to list-of-abbreviations contract. The source preserves input order, uses only the source's legal abbreviation shape, extends prefixes just enough for uniqueness, and returns the original word whenever no character is saved.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2065235829. It and the protected app source have identical TrieNode fields, `(length, first, last)` group roots, insertion counts, first-count-one traversal, omitted-character calculation, original-word threshold, formatted abbreviation, and output order; only the native class/type wrapper differs.

The single-signature workloads contain 16, 64, and 256 fixed-length words with long shared prefixes; total characters span 224 to 3584. The protected source passed all 10 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including both legal 400 boundaries. A correct pairwise common-prefix control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +1.03 and a 43.21x largest runtime ratio.

The current-targeted Approach exactly proves the collision signature, trie count meaning, minimal first-unique prefix, equivalence to repeated simultaneous extension, and safety of returning digit-free original words. It defines total input characters and accounts for grouping, both trie passes, output construction, and storage in O(S) time and space.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the three abbreviation rules in order, the shared-prefix progression example, both source input/output examples, all four constraints, distinct-word guarantee, and same-order output contract without inventing extra canonical examples.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order with their exact word lists and outputs. The missing [aa, aaa] example was restored.
The two invented samples were relabelled as trials, both formerly hidden correctness cases are now visible trials, and every dictionary contains distinct lowercase English words.
Boundaries cover one and 400 words, word lengths 2 and 400, a 398-character omitted count, singleton and multiword dictionaries, and unchanged versus abbreviated results.

Material semantics cover collision groups, different lengths and endpoints, a long common prefix that leaves no saving, minimal distinguishing prefixes, short words, multiple independent groups, unique output strings, and preservation of unsorted input order.

An independent grouped pairwise-prefix oracle verified all ten correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs. The protected implementation also agreed across 1,956 exhaustive collision dictionaries and 1,000 randomized legal dictionaries.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 224-, 896-, and 3,584-character single-signature workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
